1001:
** βολίζω**,
(βολίς) **heave the lead, take soundings,** {{NT|NT.Acts.27.28, 12th c.AD: Eustathius Episcopus Thessalonicensis 563.30}}:—_passive_, **sink in water,** {{Refs|Gp. 6.17.}}
1003:
**Βοός** and Βοές (RV, Βοάζ, Rec. Βοόζ), ὁ, indecl. (Heb. בֹּעַז),
**Boaz** (Rut.2:1): Mat.1:5, Luk.3:32.†
(From Abbott-Smith. LSJ has no entry)
1004:
** βόρβορος**, ὁ,
**mire, filth**, {{NT+7th c.BC+|7th-6th c.BC: Asius Lyricus 1, 1st c.AD(?): Heraclitus 13, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 694, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 259, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 69c, LXX.Jer.45.6, NT.2Pet.2.22. etc.: distinguished from πηλός}} **clay, moist earth**, {{Refs 2nd c.AD+|2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Prom.Es” 1}}; **sewer**, {{Refs 5th c.AD+|5th c.AD(?): Hesychius Legal icographus}}: _metaphorically_, **foul abuse**, τοσοῦτον β. κατήντλησάς μου {{Refs 2nd c.AD+|2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Lex.” 17.}}
1005:
**βορρᾶς**, -ᾶ (Attic contr. of Βορέας, the North wind personified),
[in LXX for צָפוֹן ;]
1. **Boreas, the North wind**.
2. **the north**: Luk.13:29, Rev.21:13.
† (From Abbott-Smith. LSJ has no entry)
1007:
**Βοσόρ** see Βεώρ - ὁ, indecl. (Heb. בְּעוֹר),
**Beor**, father of Balaam: 2Pe.2:15 (Rec. Βοσόρ).†
(From Abbott-Smith. LSJ has no entry)
1020:
** βρᾰδῠ-πλοέω**,
**sail slowly,** {{NT+2nd c.AD+|NT.Acts.27.7, 2nd c.AD: Artemidorus Daldianus Onirocriticus 4.30, “Anecdota Graeca - Bekker” 225.}}
1022:
** βρᾰδυτής**, ῆτος, ἡ,
**slowness, sluggishness**, βραδυτῆτί τε νωχελίη τε {{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 19.411}}; so of persons, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 932 (_anapaest meter_), 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.71, 5.75, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 109d, 4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “Characteres” 14.1: in _plural_, 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 4.141, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.246}}: literal **slowness**, opposed to τάχος, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Timaeus” 39b, compare 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Physica” 228b29.}}
1023:
** βρᾰχίων**
[_Ionic dialect_ ῐ, _Attic dialect_ ῑ], **βράχιστος**, _comparative_ and _superlative_ of βραχύς.
1029:
** βρόχος**, ὁ,
**noose, slip-knot**, {{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 11.278, 22.472, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.60, 3rd c.AD: Democritus Epigrammaticus 134, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 1222, etc.}}; **snare for birds**, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 527; θηρῶν β. 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Helena” 1169; ἁλοὺς βρόχων πλεκταῖς ἀνάγκαις 4th c.BC: Xenarchus Comicus 1.8}}; **mesh** of a net, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Cynegeticus” 2.5, etc.: _metaphorically_, β. ἀρκύων ξιφηφόροι 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hercules Furens” 729; ὡς ἂν ληφθῶσιν ἐν ταὐτῷ βρόχῳ 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 557}}; ἐν βρόχῳ τὸν τράχηλον ἔχων νομοθετεῖν 'with **a halter** round one's neck', {{Refs 4th c.BC+|4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 24.139. (βρόκχον}} should be written in {{Refs 6th c.BC+|6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 1099.)}}
1034:
** βρώσιμος**, ον,
**eatable**, {{NT+4th c.BC+|4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 479, diphthong 13, LXX.Lev.19.23, NT.Luke.24.41; ἃ καὶ κυσὶν πεινῶσιν οὐχὶ βρώσιμα “Tragica Adespota” 118.4.}}
1038:
** βυρσοδέψ-ης**, ου, ὁ,
(δέψω) **tanner**, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 44, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 221e, 3rd c.BC: Herodas Mimographus 6.88, “PPetr.” 3p.78 (3rd c.BC), 2nd c.AD: Artemidorus Daldianus Onirocriticus 2.20.}}
1040:
** βύσσος**, ἡ,
**flax**, and **the linen made from it**, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Empedocles Poeta Philosophus 93, 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 2.73, etc.}}; used of **perennial flax, Linum angustifolium**, grown in Elis, {{Refs 2nd c.AD+|2nd c.AD: Pausanias Periegeta 6.26.6}}, and of **Linum usitatissimum**, ={λίνον Ἑβραίων}, {{Refs|[prev. author] 5.5.2}}; also, in later writers, of **Indian cotton, Gossypium herbaceum**, {{Refs 2nd c.AD+|2nd c.AD(?): Pollianus Epigrammaticus 7.76, 2nd-3rd c.AD: Philostratus Sophista “Vita Apollonii” 2.20}}; and of **silk**, τὰ Σηρικὰ ἔκ τινων φλοιῶν ξαινουένης βύσσου {{Refs 1st c.BC+|1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Strabo Geographus 15.1.20.}}
1042:
**Γαββαθα** (Rec. -θᾶ), ἡ, indecl.,
**Gabbatha**, the Greek transliteration of an uncertain Aramaic word (_DB_, see word; Dalman, _Words_, 7), used as the equivalent of λιθόστρωτον, **stone pavement**: Jhn.19:13.†
(From Abbott-Smith. LSJ has no entry)
1043:
**Γαβριήλ**, ὁ, indecl. (Heb. גַּבְרִיאֵל, **hero of God**),
the archangel **Gabriel**: Luk.1:19, 26.†
(From Abbott-Smith. LSJ has no entry)
1044:
** γάγγραιν-α**, ἡ,
(γράω ?) **gangrene**, {{NT+5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “Mochl.” 33, NT.2Tim.2.17, 1st c.AD: Dioscorides (Dioscurides) Medicus 1.61, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.65d, 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 18(1).687.}}
1045:
**Γάδ**, ὁ, indecl. (Heb. גָּד),
Gad (Gen.30:11 49:13, al.): Rev.7:5.†
(From Abbott-Smith. LSJ has no entry)
1046:
**Γαδαρηνός**, -ή, -όν
(Γαδαρά, _Gadara_, the capital of Peræa),
**Gadarene, of Gadara**: Mat.8:28 (Rec. Γεργεσηνῶν), Mrk.5:1, Rec. (Edd., Γερασηνῶν), Luk.8:26, 37 Rec. (Edd., Γερασηνῶν).†
(From Abbott-Smith. LSJ has no entry)
1048:
**Γάζα -ης**, ἡ (Heb. עַזָּה),
**Gaza**, in OT, one of the five chief cities of the Philistines: Act.8:26.†
(From Abbott-Smith. LSJ has no entry)
1049:
** γᾱζο-φῠλάκιον** [λᾰ], τό,
**treasury**, {{NT+3rd c.BC+|“OGI” 225.16 (Didyma, 3rd c.BC), LXX.2Ki.23.11, 1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Strabo Geographus 7.6.1, NT.Luke.21.1, +others}}
1052:
**Γαλάτης**, -ου, ὁ (originally syn. with cl. Κέλτης; cf. 1Ma.8:2, and see next word),
**a Galatian**: Gal.3:1.†
(From Abbott-Smith. LSJ has no entry)
1053:
**Γαλατία**, -ας, ἡ,
**Galatia**;
1. a gentilic region in Asia Minor, settled by Gauls (iii/B.C).
2. **A Roman Province which included this region **(_DB_, ii, 85ff.): 1Co.16:1, Gal.1:2, 2Ti.4:10 (T, Tr., mg., Γαλλίαν), 1Pe.1:1.
† (From Abbott-Smith. LSJ has no entry)
1054:
**Γαλατικός**, -ή, -όν (see previous word),
**Galatian**, **belonging to Galatia**: Act.16:6 18:23.†
(From Abbott-Smith. LSJ has no entry)
1056:
**Γαλιλαία**, -ας, ἡ (Heb. הַגָּלִיל, _the circle, district_),
**Galilee**, the name of the northern region of Palestine in NT times: Γ. τῶν ἐθνῶν, Mat.4:15 (LXX); θάλασσα τῆς Γ., Mat.15:29 (cf. Jhn.6:1).
(From Abbott-Smith. LSJ has no entry)
1057:
**Γαλιλαῖος**, -αία, -αῖον,
**Galilæan**: Mat.26:69, Mrk.14:70, Luk.13:1, 2 22:59, 23:6, Jhn.4:45, Act.1:11 2:7 5:37.†
(From Abbott-Smith. LSJ has no entry)
1058:
**Γαλλίων**, -ωνος, ὁ,
**Gallio**, proconsul of Achaia: Act.18:12, 14 17.†
(From Abbott-Smith. LSJ has no entry)
1059:
**Γαμαλιήλ**, ὁ (Heb. גַּמְלִיאֵל),
**Gamaliel** the elder, a Pharisee and Doctor of the Law: Act.5:34 22:3.†
(From Abbott-Smith. LSJ has no entry)
1061:
** γαμ-ίσκω**,
={γαμίζω}, {{Refs 5th c.AD+|Callicratidas Philosophus cited in 5th c.AD: Stobaeus, Joannes 4.28.18:}} —_middle_ (or _passive_) in {{Refs 4th c.BC+|4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1335a20}}; ἀνδρί, of a woman, {{Refs 6th c.AD+|“PLond.” 5.1708 (6th c.AD)}}:—_passive_, {{NT|NT.Mark.12.25.}}
1066:
**Γεδεών**, ὁ, indecl. in LXX and NT, in FlJ, _Ant._, see 6, 3 and 4 -ῶνος (Heb. גִּדְעוֹן),
**Gideon** (Jdg.6-8): Heb.11:32.†
(From Abbott-Smith. LSJ has no entry)
1067:
** γέεννα**, ης, ἡ,
Hebrew **gé-hinnóm**, the **valley of Hinnom**, which represented **the place of future punishment,** {{NT|NT.Matt.5.22, +others}}
1068:
**Γεθσημασεί** (Rec. -νῆ, LTr. -νεῖ) indecl. (Heb. גֵּת שְׁמָנִי, _oil-press_),
**Gethsemane**: called in Jhn.18:1 a κῆπος, but named only in Mat.26:36, Mrk.14:32.†
(From Abbott-Smith. LSJ has no entry)
1075:
** γενεᾱλογ-έω**,
_Ionic dialect_ **γενεη-**, **trace a pedigree**, γ. γένεσιν {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.146}}; γ. ἑωυτόν **draw out** one's pedigree,{{Refs 5th c.BC+|[prev. work] 143; γ. τὴν συγγένειαν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Symposium” 4.51; γ. τινά τινος 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.894b}}; γ. τινὰ γενέσθαι, εἶναι.., {{Refs 5th c.BC+|[prev. author] “Lyc.” 1, 2nd c.AD: Pausanias Periegeta 5.14.9; περί τινος 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Salt.” 7: _absolutely_, οἱ -λογοῦντες 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 15.180, 4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “Characteres” 28.2}}:—_passive_, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ ἑπταμήνου” 4; ταῦτα μέν νυν γεγενεηλόγηται 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.54; τὰ νυνδὴ γενεαλογηθέντα 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Timaeus” 23b}}; γενεαλογούμενος ἔκ τινος {{NT|NT.Heb.7.6}}; ἐγενεαλογήθη (_impersonal_) **the genealogy was reckoned**, {{LXX|LXX.1Ch.5.1.}}
1076:
** γενεᾱλογ-ία**, ἡ,
**tracing a pedigree**, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Cratylus” 396c, +others: in _plural_, 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 11.8}}; title of work by Hecataeus; γ. καὶ μῦθοι {{NT+2nd c.BC+|2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 9.2.1, cf. NT.1Tim.1.4, 4th c.AD: Julianus Imperator “Orationes” 7.205c.}}
1079:
** γενετ-ή**, ἡ,
={γενεά} II.3, ἐκ γενετῆς from **the hour of birth**, {{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.535, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 18.6; εὐθὺς ἐκ γ. 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Nicomachea” 1144b6; opposed to δι᾽ ἔθος, [prev. work] 1154a33}}; later ἀπὸ γενετῆς {{Refs 4th c.AD+|4th c.AD: Iamblichus Philosophus “de vita Pythagorica” 30.171.}}
1082:
**Γεννησαρέτ** (Rec. Γενησ-, Mk, l.with; Targ. גְּנֵיסַר),
[in LXX: Γεννησάρ (as in some MSS. Mt, Mk), 1Ma.11:67 * ;]
**Gennesaret**, a fertile plain on W. shore of the Sea of Galilee; ἡ γῆ, Mat.14:34, Mrk.6:53; ἡ λίμνη (יָם כִּנֶּרֶת, Num.34:11, elsewhere ἡ θάλασσα τ. Γαλιλαίας, Mrk.1:16; ἡ θ. τ. Τιβεριάδος, Jhn.6:1), Luk.5:1.†
(From Abbott-Smith. LSJ has no entry)
1086:
**Γεργασηνός**, -ή, -όν,
**Gerasene, of Gerasa**, not the G. of Decapolis, 30 m. S.E. of the Lake, but a Gerasa or Gergesa (perh. the mod. _Kersa_) on E. shore; as subst., pl. οἱ Γ., Mrk.5:1, Luk.8:26, 37 (Γεργεσηνῶν, RV, mg. 1; Γαδαρηνῶν, RV, mg. 2).†
(From Abbott-Smith. LSJ has no entry)
1092:
** γεωργ-ός**, όν,
(γῆ, ἔργον) **tilling the ground**, βοίδιον {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 1036}}; **fertilizing**, Νεῖλος {{Refs 4th c.AD+|4th c.AD: Libanius Sophista “Orationes” 13.39:}} —as _substantive_, γεωργός, ὁ, **husbandman**, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.18, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Pax” 296, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 276b, etc.}}; οἱ γ., opposed to οἱ μισθαρνοῦντες, {{Refs 4th c.BC+|4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1296b28}}; but γ., opposed to ὁ δεσπότης τοῦ χωρίου, {{Refs|“IG” 22.1100}}; so of vine-dressers, gardeners, etc., {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 178d, 2nd-3rd c.AD: Aelianus “De Natura Animalium - Ar.Byzantine Epit.” 7.28}}; γ. ὄχλος **the peasantry**, {{Refs 1st c.BC+|1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 10.53}}; γ. βίος probably in {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Pax” 589; δένδρων ὧν γ. αἵδε αἱ χεῖρες 2nd-3rd c.AD: Philostratus Sophista “Vita Apollonii” 2.26.}}
